Subject: Processing footprint & erasure responsibility — quick Qs

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency numbers. We have a short list of compliance items before we move to procurement. Could you confirm the following at a high level so I can route to our security/legal folks?

1) Where are inference requests executed by default (regions)? Are there per-tenant pins?
2) Which subprocessors are involved in request execution, KV/prefix caching, and long-term logs?
3) What triggers data deletion for inference inputs, KV cache, and audit logs? Can we get SLA windows?
4) How do you handle cross-border fallbacks (e.g., if a region is out of capacity and requests route elsewhere)?
5) Any docs/evidence we can share with our auditors?

I attached our short questionnaire (halo-data-questionnaire.xlsx) with a couple of specific asks — if you can return the matrix and a draft DPA redline we can review.

Appreciate a concise reply — our timeline is tight (SOW/PO in the next 3–4 weeks).

Best,
Elena Novak
Director, IT Risk & Compliance
Halo Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Elena — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below so your legal/security can triage; Marissa (solutions) is cc'd with the residency matrix and DPA draft attached.

Summary (short):
- Default execution: US-East (primary) with configurable region pins per customer (we can pin to single region on Dedicated/Private).
- Subprocessors: runtime (Redwood runtime), cloud infra (AWS/GCP), monitoring/logging (Datadog for metrics, optional S3 logging). Detailed list in attached matrix.
- Deletion triggers: immediate for per-request transient data (after response emitted), KV cache TTL configurable (default 24h), audit logs retention configurable (30/90/365 days tiers). We provide erase APIs and documented workflows.
- Cross-border fallback: policy-driven — by default we prefer same-region capacity; if capacity is constrained we fall back to compatible variants in same region tier or nearest region per routing policy; fallbacks can be disabled for compliance-sensitive customers.
- Evidence: attached residency matrix, DPA draft; we can assemble an audit pack (SOC 2 summary, subprocessors list, network diagrams) on request.

Attachments: redwood-residency-matrix.pdf (matrix + subprocessor roster), redwood-dpa-draft.pdf (initial redline).

Next steps: If you want, Marissa can provide a short technical note on cache semantics and erase flow today, and Karthik (on infra) can add the low-level KV/eviction details.

Happy to jump on a 30m call if that helps — are you available this afternoon?

Regards,

Hi Elena — adding some more concrete details so your security team has what they need. I pulled the relevant lines into bullets to keep it scannable.

1) Regions & pinning
- Hosted: default tenancy runs in US-East (us-east-1); secondary regions available (us-west-2, eu-west-1) depending on account region.
- Dedicated/Private: customer can pin inference execution to a single region or VPC; Private (on-prem) keeps everything inside customer network.

2) Subprocessors & roles
- Redwood runtime (redwood-inference-runtime) — handles tokenization, model execution, KV cache management. (Redwood-managed, runs in customer region for pinned accounts.)
- Cloud infra: AWS (EC2/GPU instances, S3 for optional archival), GCP for certain regions — specific provider depends on the region selected.
- Monitoring & metrics: Datadog (metrics/traces only; sensitive logs excluded unless enabled).
- Logging/archives: optional S3 buckets (customer-owned or Redwood-managed depending on account config).
- Third-party tooling: OpenTelemetry for traces, HashiCorp Vault/KMS for key management integrations.

3) Deletion semantics & SLAs
- Per-request payloads: transient; we drop input payloads from memory after response generation; no persistent store unless customer enables logging. Effective deletion: immediate at response completion.
- KV / prefix cache: controlled TTL (default 24 hours), customer-configurable down to immediate eviction. We expose an erase API (DELETE /v1/cache/{namespace}) — SLA for purge from in-memory nodes is typically seconds; full cluster eviction propagation to all nodes and optional on-disk caches: up to 15 minutes under normal conditions.
- Audit logs & usage archives: configurable retention tiers (30/90/365). Deletion requests for archives: processed within 5 business days for managed archives; for customer-owned storage we provide instructions and verification artifacts.

4) Cross-border fallback & routing policy
- Routing policy is policy-first: prefer same-region; if capacity unavailable we route to a compatible local variant. For customers with strict residency requirements we can disable cross-region fallback.
- All cross-region routing is logged; we can provide per-request routing metadata in trace outputs for audit.

Technical footnote from Karthik (included inline):

On Fri, 25 Sep 2027 at 12:05, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Cache eviction & KV details:
> - In-memory KV is sharded with per-shard compaction. Eviction propagation uses a gossip protocol; local purge is immediate, cluster-wide convergence < 15 minutes typical.
> - If a request is served from a warm KV from another region during fallback, the request metadata contains the origin-region and cache-hit flag; that metadata is stored in ephemeral traces (not in long-term logs) unless logging is enabled.
> - For customers requiring cryptographic erasure evidence we support key-rotation-based proofs for S3 archives and can provide signed deletion receipts for managed archives.
>
> - Note: For Private deployments the runtime and caches never leave the customer network unless configured otherwise.

5) Evidence & artifacts we can provide (short list)
- Residency matrix (attached) with per-region subprocessors and network egress points.
- SOC 2 summary and control mappings.
- DPA redline (attached) and standard subprocessors list.
- Per-request trace sample (sanitized) showing routing metadata if you want to validate fallback behavior.

If you send back the questionnaire rows that are highest priority we will populate them in the matrix and return the audit pack.

Thanks,
